title: Beruriah and the Troublesome Neighbors
text:
Rabbi Meir was one of the great sages of the second century, and his wife Beruriah was famous in her own right for her learning, which is unusual in the records of that age.

In their neighborhood lived some hoodlums who caused Rabbi Meir a great deal of grief. They harassed him so much that he began to pray that they would die.

Beruriah heard him and objected. "What are you thinking?" she asked. "Is it because it is written in the Psalms, 'Let sins cease from the earth'? It does not say 'sinners', it says 'sins'. And look at the end of the same verse: 'and the wicked will be no more.' Once the sins have ended, there will be no more wicked people. Pray for them instead, that they turn back from their ways, and then they will be wicked no longer."

Rabbi Meir took her advice. He prayed for them to change rather than to perish, and the Talmud reports that they repented.
lesson: When someone is making your life hard, aim at ending the harmful behavior, not at destroying the person. People can change, and enemies can become neighbors again.
